articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launches toward Phobos, marking an ambitious exploration of Mars's mysterious moon.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration mission prepares for launch on an H3 rocket, embarking on a historic journey to explore the enigmatic moons of Mars.

articles.title: Lumina simulation brings the early universe to life on a record-breaking scale
articles.description: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and Nancy Roman Space Telescope are revealing the universe's earliest chapters in detail. To help astronomers understand what they are seeing, researchers at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian have developed "Lumina," one of the largest and most detailed simulations ever created of the early universe.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The Lumina simulation creates a record-breaking visualization of the early universe, complementing revelations from JWST and the Nancy Roman Space Telescope.

articles.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy. Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away. One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.
articles.summary: Astronomers have made a landmark discovery of three actively feeding supermassive black holes within a single galaxy from the early Universe, over 12.5 billion light-years away.

articles.title: Astronomers may have discovered the first moon beyond our Solar System
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of a bizarre, potentially historic discovery: the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System. Unlike familiar moons, this mysterious object is at least as massive as Jupiter and orbits a brown dwarf, which itself circles a star. The unusual arrangement challenges traditional definitions of planets and moons, leaving scientists unsure what to call it.
articles.summary: Researchers have uncovered compelling evidence of what may be the first moon ever detected orbiting an exoplanet, a historic breakthrough in planetary science.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Offers Clues to Protect Crews From Mars Dust
articles.description: Over 1,645 Martian days, NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover measured the fine and ultrafine Martian dust particles found clinging to samples of spacesuit materials that are carried aboard the rover, including some that are small enough to penetrate the lungs and enter the bloodstream. The findings will be published Tuesday, Oct. 27, in the Proceedings of […]
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has gathered critical data on Martian dust particles over its mission, providing essential insights for protecting future human crews on Mars.

articles.title: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.description:
Image:
			Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.summary: A stunning image captures the stellar nursery where stars are actively forming within a nebula, showcasing the cosmic process of stellar birth.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates eight years in flight on its landmark mission to Mercury, advancing our understanding of the solar system's innermost planet.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope discovers its first previously unknown comet, demonstrating the mission's powerful capability to detect new celestial objects.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The ESA's Solar Orbiter spacecraft flies through a magnetic switchback in the solar wind, solving mysteries about mysterious structures in the Sun's corona.

articles.title: A Huge and Powerful New Simulation Helps Explain the Universe's Reionization
articles.description: Cosmologists have another powerful simulation to work with. Lumina is the one of the largest and most detailed cosmological simulations yet and runs on the Frontier supercomputer. It's larger and more detailed than Illustris TNG.
articles.summary: The Lumina simulation represents one of the largest and most detailed cosmological models ever created, advancing our understanding of the universe's reionization period.

articles.title: JWST and ALMA reveal a dusty, rapidly growing black hole in the early universe
articles.description: A new study reveals a dust-reddened quasar from a time when the universe was less than a billion years old. Located at a redshift of 6.5488, the object J1440+0019 contains a rapidly accreting supermassive black hole with a mass of about 1.1 billion suns. The paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 9.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: JWST and ALMA observations have revealed a rapidly growing dust-reddened black hole and quasar from when the universe was less than a billion years old.

articles.title: Milky Way's disk grew 'upside down,' with younger stars forming in ever-thinner layers
articles.description: The Milky Way is home to hundreds of billions of stars arranged in a glorious spiral pattern. But beyond the obvious spiral, our galaxy has other physical characteristics. It's divided into a galactic bulge, a galactic disk and a galactic halo.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: New research reveals the Milky Way's disk grew in an unexpected 'upside down' pattern, with younger stars forming in progressively thinner layers—challenging our understanding of galactic evolution.

articles.title: NASA’s asteroid Bennu samples reveal a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
articles.description: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are rewriting scientists' understanding of how our Solar System formed. New evidence suggests that Bennu was born where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.
articles.summary: Samples from NASA's asteroid Bennu mission are revealing 4.5-billion-year-old secrets that fundamentally reshape our understanding of Solar System formation.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover a mysterious magnetic web above the Sun
articles.description: The Sun’s seemingly peaceful regions are hiding a surprisingly complex magnetic world. Using a balloon-borne telescope high above Earth, scientists discovered delicate, thread-like magnetic structures woven through the solar atmosphere, apparently shaped by twisting motions on the Sun’s surface. They also mapped magnetic fields inside towering jets of solar material, revealing how those fields change with height.
articles.summary: Using advanced balloon-borne telescope technology, astronomers have discovered a surprisingly complex magnetic web hidden above the Sun's seemingly peaceful regions.

articles.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
articles.description: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe’s expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works.
articles.summary: An analysis of nearly 3,000 exploding stars reveals new evidence about dark energy and its role in the Universe's accelerating expansion.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 26, 2004: Cassini spacecraft takes 1st-ever closeup photos of Saturn moon Titan
articles.description: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft took the first close-up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: On October 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft captured the first close-up images of Saturn's moon Titan, a landmark achievement in planetary exploration.

articles.title: Record breaker! Astronomers spot powerful cosmic explosion that lasted 27 days
articles.description: Astronomers have spotted a remarkable gamma-ray burst  that's a real Incredible Hulk compared to other cosmic explosions of the same type.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a remarkably long-lasting gamma-ray burst that persisted for 27 days, representing an exceptional cosmic explosion event. This record-breaking observation expands our understanding of high-energy astrophysical phenomena.

articles.title: SpaceX ignites giant Super Heavy booster engines ahead of daring Starship launch (video)
articles.description: SpaceX conducted a static-fire test with its Super Heavy boosters B22 on Sunday (Oct. 25), beginning a test campaign to ready the giant rocket for Starship's Flight Test 15.
articles.summary: SpaceX successfully conducted a static-fire test of its Super Heavy booster B22, marking progress toward the next Starship launch. This test campaign demonstrates advancing capabilities for the company's ambitious launch vehicle development.

articles.title: NASA JPL Looks to Next 90 Years of Innovation, Exploration
articles.description: Interstellar probes. Lunar drones. Helicopters on Mars. When a group of Caltech graduate students and enthusiasts began conducting rocket-propulsion tests in Pasadena’s Arroyo Seco on Oct. 31, 1936, they had no idea that their work marked the inception of the…
articles.summary: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory looks toward the next 90 years of innovation with ambitious projects including interstellar probes, lunar drones, and Mars helicopters. This forward-looking vision showcases humanity's expanding capabilities for space exploration.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the s…
articles.summary: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar, a newly recognized class of cosmic objects distinct from larger extragalactic blazars. This discovery expands our catalog of high-energy astrophysical phenomena.

Its two flat […]
articles.summary: NASA's NEO Surveyor mission undergoes component inspection, with technicians verifying the large sunshade assembly that will help detect near-Earth objects.

articles.title: Solar Cells Inspected on NASA’s NEO Surveyor
articles.description: Description The large sunshade of NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor mission is inspected by a technician at BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems in Boulder, Colorado, in late July.  Built by Applied Aerospace in Stockton, California, the sunshade structure was outfitted with its solar cells by SolAero Technologies in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in January. Environmental […]
articles.summary: Solar cells on NASA's NEO Surveyor mission are inspected to ensure optimal performance for the near-Earth object detection mission.

articles.title: NASA SEES Interns Tackle Real-World Challenges in Lunar Exploration
articles.description: The NASA STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) Enhancement in Earth Science (SEES) Internship Program at the University of Texas Center for Space Research places high school students on small, mission-focused research teams mentored by NASA, academic, and industry experts. During summer 2026, the SEES Mission Architecture Tool for Research, Integration, and eXploration (MATRIX) team […]
articles.summary: NASA's SEES Internship Program engages STEM students in solving real-world challenges for lunar exploration missions.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media to Moon Landing Simulation Experience in California
articles.description: Members of the media are invited to tour a new lunar landing simulator at NASA’s Ames Research Center in California's Silicon Valley on Thursday, Oct. 29, and Friday, Oct. 30.
articles.summary: NASA opens a new lunar landing simulator at Ames Research Center, allowing media and public to experience the challenges of Moon landing operations.

articles.title: Where winds blow and lava flows
articles.description:

articles.summary: A captivating image showcases the dynamic processes of wind and lava on a planetary or lunar surface, revealing the powerful forces shaping worlds.

articles.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
articles.description: Scientists using the European Space Agency's Mars Express, in combination with a state-of-the-art meteorological model of the Red Planet, have found that there may be some very exotic physics behind Mars’s most curious cloud.
articles.summary: European Space Agency's Mars Express has revealed surprising new characteristics about Mars's unusual atmospheric cloud formations using advanced meteorological modeling.

articles.title: A Brief-ish History of METI. Part I: Early Ideas and Experiments
articles.description: For as long as scientists have conducted SETI (Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence) experiments, parallel efforts in Messaging Extraterrestrial Intelligence (METI) have also been mounted. In this series, we'll take a look at the major milestones in this field of study.
articles.summary: Scientists have developed parallel messaging initiatives alongside traditional SETI experiments, exploring humanity's efforts to communicate with potential extraterrestrial civilizations.

articles.title: Scientists Can Now Spot Hidden Sunspots on the Solar Far Side
articles.description: Unlike the Moon, the Sun is constantly rotating from our perspective - but we still only see half of it at any given time. Since it takes 27 days to complete a full rotation, that leaves plenty of time for changes to happen to the side we can’t see that could directly impact Earth’s own space weather a few weeks later. Now a team of physicists led by Bibhuti Kumar Jha of the Southwest Research Institute has published a paper in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series that uses probability to map out what might be happening on the far side of the Sun, even if we can’t see it directly.
articles.summary: Scientists have developed new techniques to detect and observe hidden sunspots on the far side of the Sun that are invisible from Earth.

articles.title: Parker Solar Probe Spots Twisted Magnetic Braids Growing in the Solar Wind
articles.description: The magnetic environment around the Sun is a jumbled mess of chaotic fields and streams of charged particles. Recently we’ve been getting at least slightly better at mapping out its complexity, thanks in large part to data collected by missions like the Parker Solar Probe and Solar Orbiter. But there’s still a large grey area surrounding the interface between the large scale hydrodynamic properties of plasmas and the microscopic properties of individual ions, and scientists believe understanding large scale features of the Sun, such as why its corona is so much hotter than its surface, may rely on our knowledge of that interface. A new paper that directly tackles some of the outstanding questions about that interface was recently published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters by Masatomi Iizawa of the Technical University of Braunschweig and his co-authors.
articles.summary: NASA's Parker Solar Probe has discovered twisted magnetic field structures forming in the solar wind around the Sun.
